title: Trace Tables
goals: Trace variable values before and after each loop iteration
Use the excluded stop value in range correctly
Explain initialization and test zero one and several iterations
vocabulary: A block of instructions that can run repeatedly
One execution of a loop body
A variable that keeps a running result
Giving a variable its starting value
A record of variable values as instructions execute

worked_example.title: Test how many times the body runs

blocks.text: With one argument, range starts at zero. range(4) supplies four values but none is 4. If the worked script uses range(1, 1), the body never runs and the initialized total remains 0. Do not rely on a variable first assigned inside a loop: a zero-iteration run might never assign it.

blocks.label: Replace range(1, 4) with range(1, 3) in the worked script. Predict the supplied values and final total. What stop value is needed to include 3?

guided_practice.title: Trace before running
guided_practice.prompt: Copy the worked script. Change the range to range(2, 5). Record turn, total before and total after each iteration. Predict the single output, then run and compare.
guided_practice.answer: Rows are 2 / 0 / 2, 3 / 2 / 5, 4 / 5 / 9. Final output 9. Keep the observed result distinct from the prediction.

independent_case.title: Build a repeated addition independently
independent_case.task: A box starts with 5 counters. Each round adds 2 counters. Use rounds = 3, an initialized total and for turn in range(rounds). Print the final total once after the loop. Trace the totals and predict fresh runs with rounds 0, 1 and 3. Assume rounds is a nonnegative integer.
independent_case.answer: Initialize total = 5 before the loop; add 2 inside it. For three rounds, turn values 0, 1, 2 give totals 7, 9, 11. Final outputs for 0, 1, 3 rounds are 5, 7, 11. Print is unindented.
independent_case.source: primary source W4, first curriculum occurrence

misconceptions: List the supplied values before tracing; range(1, 4) excludes 4.
Resetting the accumulator loses earlier work.
An unindented print repeats with the body
Zero iterations mean the entire program does nothing
Initialization and statements after the loop still execute.

blocks.title: Python 3 code
blocks.text:
total = 0
for turn in range(1, 4):
    total = total + turn
print(total)

blocks.title: State after each addition
blocks.caption: Initialize total to 0 before the loop. The unindented print runs once afterward.

blocks.text: The output is 6. Before the first iteration, total is 0. Each assignment reads the previous total and adds the current turn. After turn 3, the range is exhausted, so execution continues after the loop. The table records state; it does not create extra instructions.
